newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end at 7-yr high on electronics surge.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end at 7-yr high on electronics surge.

text.p: A strong rebound by electronics pushed Taiwan shares to a seven-year high close on Monday despite some unease over Taipei's controversial staging of large-scale war games on Monday and Tuesday, brokers said.
The index surged to as high as 8,940.88 points and ended at 8,925.12, a gain of 91.29 points or 1.03 percent.
That surpassed a 8,922.67 close on May 9, 1990. The index has not closed higher since ending at 8,948.49 on May 8, 1990.
Turnover was heavy at T$159.3 billion, but much below an all-time high T$251 billion marked on Thursday.

Electronics, which suffered profit-taking on Saturday, rebounded a bullish 5.35 percent after chip giant Taiwan Semiconductor said on Monday it would raise its 1997 sales and profit targets by more than 20 percent within 10 days due to improving performance.

"Earlier, many (investors) said electronics had been surging on dreams of a sound 1998 semiconductor outlook, but now Taiwan Semiconductor's move had made the dreams a reality," said independent analyst Michael Hung.
Taiwan Semiconductor was up the daily seven percent limit to close at T$115.5.
Rival chipamkers United Microelectronics, Winbond and Mosel all were limit up to T$T$113, T$54.5 and T$87.5, respectively.

"Because of an expected sound third quarter recovery, other chipmakers...likely will follow Taiwan Semiconductor's plan and raise their 1997 profit and sales targets," said HSBC James Capel research manager Alex Chen.

The index rose despite controversy over Taiwan's holding of two days of large-scale war games from Monday. The United States had said the move could needlessly rile Taiwan's arch rival, China, on the eve of Hong Kong's July 1 handover to Beijing.
